subject: SSQ: telemetry & PII dataflow clarifications (pseudonymization + access controls)
messages:
From: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SSQ — telemetry, PII in inference calls, and dataflow diagram request

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the SSQ draft you shared last week. A few follow-ups from our privacy and security team while we validate Redwood for inference calls inside our clinical workflow:

- Can you confirm exactly which request/response fields are considered PII vs. non-PII for the hosted API (we need a per-field mapping).
- For telemetry and inference logs: are user identifiers pseudonymized before storage? If so, what algorithm/derivation is used and can you provide the pseudonymization matrix?
- Access controls: who at Redwood can view raw request payloads? Please list roles and whether access is recorded in audit logs.
- Cross-border transfer question: if a request originates in EU, does any component of the pipeline route tokens through a US-based service? If yes, what legal mechanism (SCCs, BCR, etc.) covers that?

We'd like an updated dataflow diagram that highlights where PII is encountered and where pseudonymization/redaction occurs. Also attaching our intake checklist — can you return the completed matrix as an Excel table and a redlined DPA if there are changes?

Attachments from Acme: Acme_SSQ_Checklist.xlsx (referenced)

Can you get us a response by Friday so we can move to our security review? If helpful let's also schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough.

Thanks,
Lina Torres
Director, Privacy & Risk
AcmeHealth

Subject: Re: SSQ — telemetry, PII in inference calls, and dataflow diagram request

Hi Lina —

Appreciate the detailed asks. Quick summary of what we'll deliver by Thursday EOD (so you have it before Friday review):

1) Field-level PII mapping (CSV/Excel) that marks request/response fields as PII / quasi-ID / non-PII + examples.
2) Pseudonymization matrix (Excel) with algorithm notes. We use reversible KMS-wrapped tokenization for customer identifiers in telemetry and one-way hashing for ephemeral session ids; details and caveats will be in the doc.
3) Dataflow diagram (PDF) showing exactly where data is cached, tokenized, redacted, and where telemetry is emitted.
4) Access control list + audit log retention summary (roles that can `view_payloads`, `download_exports`, and the corresponding logging hooks).
5) Cross-border and transfer attachments explaining routing and relied legal mechanisms.

We're attaching a draft diagram and a starter pseudonymization matrix for you to review (see attachments). Also, we've flagged a couple of DPA items for your legal team — I'll include redlines separately.

Would you be available for a 30-min walkthrough Thursday at 10am PT? If not, propose a slot and we'll accommodate.

Best,
Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SSQ — telemetry, PII in inference calls, and dataflow diagram request

Lina — quick tech note to supplement Jordan's doc:

- Telemetry emission: we separate telemetry into 3 tiers: (1) request-level metadata (headers, model id, latency buckets), (2) token-level metrics (counts, perplexity aggregates) — token-level content is not stored, and (3) optional request/response dumps (customer-enabled for debugging).
- Customer-enabled dumps are stored in a separate, time-limited artifact store and are encrypted with a customer-specific KMS key when requested (we record the kseq id).
- Pseudonymization: for identifiers we use a KMS-wrapped reversible token (AES-GCM + KMS-wrapping) with an HMAC prefix for collision checks. Ephemeral session ids are hashed with SHA-256 + salt per-region.
- Access: only the roles `SRE-investigations`, `SE-support-readonly`, and Legal Compliance (rare, approval workflow) have the ability to request decrypted dumps. All access requests create a ticket and a corresponding audit entry (ticket id recorded).

I'll add these as bullets in the matrix we send. One caveat: if you plan to enable full request/response dumps as part of debugging, we recommend scoping the TTL to 72 hours and limiting to a bounded dataset.

— Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lina Torres <lina.torres@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SSQ — telemetry, PII in inference calls, and dataflow diagram request

Hi Lina, Jordan —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled the artifacts together. Attached are: the finalized field-level mapping (SSQ_Field_Mapping.csv), the pseudonymization-matrix.xlsx with implementation notes, and an updated dataflow PDF annotated with where we apply pseudonymization, KV cache boundaries, and audit hooks.

A couple of operational points for Acme to note:
- If you require that we never persist explicit patient identifiers in telemetry at all, we can enable an inbound redaction hook that strips configured fields at the edge — this will increase CPU time and may affect tail latency by ~5–15ms depending on batch sizes.
- For EU-origin traffic: routing policy pins inference to EU-hosted pools by default; however, control-plane operations (or some telemetry aggregation tasks) may route metadata to the US. We provide SCCs for cross-border processing and can include an appendix on our SCC reliance.
- Audit logs: immutable logs are retained for 365 days by default; extended retention is available as an add-on.

Next steps we propose:
1) Review attached matrix and confirm whether you want edge redaction enabled.
2) Legal review the redlined DPA (we've uploaded to DocuSign for convenience).
3) 30-min walkthrough to go over the diagram and controls.

I've penciled a slot: Thu 16 Aug 2028 10:00am PT. Jordan — please confirm and send calendar invite to Lina.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SSQ_Field_Mapping.csv, pseudonymization-matrix.xlsx, SSQ_Dataflow_v2.pdf, redlines_dpa_acme_2028.docx

Grace/Jordan/Marcus —

Received — thank you. The artifacts look comprehensive and the pseudonymization approach aligns with our expectations. A few quick items from the Acme privacy team after a skim:

- We'd like edge redaction enabled for patient_id and patient_email; please include an estimate of expected latency impact for our normal traffic pattern (we'll share QPS shortly).
- Please confirm that audit log entries related to `view_payloads` include the ticket id and approver identity (we need both for our compliance attestations).
- Legal will run the redlined DPA and we will respond via DocuSign (no blockers yet).

We'll take the 10:00am PT slot — Lina and one engineer (Jeff Sullivan) will join. Please send a calendar invite and the Drive links. Once the redlines are cleared we can move the file to our onboarding queue.

Best,
Lina Torres
Director, Privacy & Risk
AcmeHealth
